question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(X+Y)],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}},\, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le x, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y).
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le x\},$ where $f(x)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270831/assets/a4f7e4e3f5e6a46fdc1b61a40986aec7b47fe75b37c8f042497aa0f3a0969f30.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(X+Y)] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\cdot \frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)]_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)]}_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )]-0 \\  & =\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
